assessments.reasoning: Section 10.1.2 says FORK creates a new process executing the named procedure and returns a PROCESS value. JOIN and RETURN form a rendezvous in either order. On the pair, the returning process is deleted and the joining process continues with the results when present.

challenge.method: Check both rendezvous orders, the empty result clause, repeated JOIN, catch clauses, detach and the internal monitor-procedure exclusion on printed page 158.
challenge.results: The source allows either order and an empty RETURNS clause. A repeat JOIN is undefined, the discussed catch phrase does not catch signals inside the forked procedure, and an internal monitor-procedure target is excluded. Separate from the documented single normal join, a detached process need not be joined.

limitations: This review concerns valid target procedures and a single normal return and join. No scheduling order, detached-process lifecycle or compiler execution was inferred.
